minutes.headline: Conservation Commission endorsed an Earth Day trail cleanup, approved several wetland filings, and pressed two shoreline enforcement cases.
minutes.summary: The commission, meeting by Zoom, endorsed an April 24 Earth Day trail cleanup proposed by Mary Wilson. It heard and voted on wetland filings: a dock, a stormwater amendment, a Marshall Park restroom, a tree removal and a culvert replacement. It asked the town to put three foreclosed parcels under its care and control. Two lakeside enforcement matters (a tree-replacement plan and a grading and clearing violation) were continued with requests for diagrams, photos and overlays.

budget_items.topic: Timber rights fund purchase order for trash bags
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said an existing purchase order at a local store, funded from the timber rights fund, could cover trash bags for the cleanup.
The ledger publisher agreed to donate a quarter page ad for the Earth Day event.

budget_items.topic: Open space ad hoc committee funding
budget_items.what_was_said: The open space ad hoc committee has no power beyond recommendations, and a developer gave it a donation.
An applicant said an additional culvert requirement and its change cost him tens of thousands of dollars.
The applicant said cutting trees, leveling and replanting is expensive, which is why he wants to do it piece by piece.

decisions.decision: Chair agreed a member may meet with the Hickory Hills land and resources head about tree approaches, with no decisions made without bringing them to the commission.
Chair's view that Snow Riders' trail equipment use for maintenance needs no formal vote; Earth Day volunteers to use a dedicated email address.
Review and revocation of the old tax-title parcel list deferred to the first May meeting; open space liaison question also deferred to that meeting pending whether a non-member can serve.
A member offered to go on site with the agent and draw a scale plan of stumps and suggested replacement plantings for the Summergin tree-replacement matter.
McGirt matter continued to next meeting: member to find pictures, applicant to provide topography overlay, engineer narratives on driveway width and culvert, applicant to submit photos.
Hollis Road maintenance bid specs to wait for the new DPW director starting in May.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted to request that three foreclosed tax-title parcels be placed under its care and control; the chair noted this needs town meeting.
The commission approved a notice of intent for the Marshall Park restroom and septic system, with two special conditions.
It approved a culvert replacement at Arbor and Page Street and the Emke notice of intent without the pergola.
Two lakeside enforcement matters, the McGirt grading and clearing case and the Summergin tree-replacement plan, were continued with requests for diagrams, photos and overlays.
The commission endorsed an April 24 Earth Day trail cleanup, and it approved several smaller filings, including a dock, rain gardens and tree removals.

why_it_matters: Putting tax-title parcels under conservation care and control would change who manages that land, and it would take a town meeting vote residents may be asked to cast.
The commission's wetland and shoreline rulings set the conditions on building and tree removal near water in town, and the unresolved enforcement cases show where those rules are still being tested.
watch_next: Review and revocation of the old tax-title parcel list, and the open space liaison question, were deferred to the first May meeting.
The McGirt enforcement matter returns at the next meeting, pending photos, a topography overlay and engineer narratives.
